dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: May the Anemo Archon protect you, Deacon Dahlia. It has been some time since we last met. I did not expect your first request to be for me to hear your confession.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: You are the closest to our god here in the Church of Favonius. I would be honored to have you hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: I suspect that I am, in truth, furthest away. How else would I be able to see his divine glory in full?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Is that so? I thought you might say that each of us should try our best to draw nearer to him, for the eye of the hurricane is often the quietest spot of all.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: I believe that Barbatos, in his mercy, will not allow the hurricane to sweep through Mondstadt. Amidst the warm breezes he sends, what we should do is go beyond our city's walls and enjoy his many blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Well, you certainly did that. But the winds in Nod-Krai must be much colder than those in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Of course. And it's not as if the wind that blows through that land is Favonian in nature.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Hmm. We seem to have visitors outside, Deaconess Barbara among them. Are they here for confession as well?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Indeed. In a way, though, I suspect I'm better suited than she is to be the first to seek confession from you.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Deaconess Barbara is a diligent sister. May the Anemo Archon protect her as well. If you would be so kind, please pass on the message that I will hear her confession anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Could you not tell her yourself, sir?

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: I have thought about this as well, Deacon Dahlia. But a wind that has been away from home so long must take its time to find the flowers it once nurtured.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: So, the first thing you did was to wait here at the Cathedral?

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: I went home as soon as I could, but Jean was working overtime at the Knights' headquarters, and Barbara had already gone to the Cathedral, so... *sigh* Anyway, you may begin, Deacon Dahlia.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Bless me, Anemo Archon, for I have sinned. It has been two weeks since my last confession. I just lied to Deaconess Barbara, hiding the truth that Venti is in fact Barbatos from her.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: You can tell her the truth, you know. Barbatos said so himself.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I actually did, but she warned me that I'd be picking every last weed from the Cathedral's front lawn if I said that again. Maybe you could give it a try...?

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: For the sake of our bond as parent and child... perhaps it might be best if Barbatos revealed that truth to the faithful in person. Anyway, Deacon Dahlia, please continue.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Five days ago, I offended the Archon by accidentally losing to Venti in a game of Genius Invokation TCG.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: According to the rules we set, if he won, I would treat him to a drink — but if he lost, he'd treat himself to two drinks as punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: I am sure you upheld the virtue of honesty with regard to this rule, and ensured that Venti did so as well.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Indeed I did. Following his victory, I confessed to him right there and then, before treating him to three drinks. He absolved me, along with the others drinking nearby who were egging us on.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: May he absolve us all, especially Charles. Out of any of us, he offends our Archon the most.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Finally, I confess to an act of laziness that took place seven days ago. While working alongside Sister Rosaria and Deaconess Barbara, Rosaria and I sneaked off to grab a drink.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: ...Should you not, therefore, be confessing to day-drinking as well?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: No, I myself did not drink wine. Sister Rosaria drank double, and Charles served me some juice on the side.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Mmm... The sin of drinking immoderately in the day, then. What about Deaconess Barbara?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: She had finished plucking the weeds by the time we returned, and had already made a start on wiping the windows. I brought her some juice.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: And you and Sister Rosaria observed the principle of kindness and generosity by taking the cloth from her hands, I trust?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: We did. Sister Rosaria and I finished the rest together.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Thank you. If word had reached Frederica that Barbara had been made to wipe all the windows in the Cathedral by herself, she'd come and flip my desk right over.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Well, a shame that she's still out on her mission, so she can't come to see you right now... Anyway. That concludes my confession, Cardinal.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Alright. In that case, copy the Favonian Liturgy three times, and the Proverbs six. May the Anemo Archon protect you, Deacon Dahlia.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: May he protect us all. That said, are you also unaware of Ms. Frederica's whereabouts? I recall that you and Mr. Varka set off for Nod-Krai together... Ah, by the way, I must also "confess" — I'm asking this on Deaconess Barbara's behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Perhaps Varka might know. But considering how dangerous things were in Nod-Krai, I doubt he had time to keep track of her whereabouts either.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: The letters we exchange mostly contain pleasantries, but it comforts me to know that she is well. I sent word of this home, so Barbara knows as well.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: I would say that Jean would know Frederica's whereabouts best. But she shoulders a heavy responsibility... Heh, this family of ours...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I believe you need not worry, Cardinal. By the Anemo Archon's grace, the thousand winds that blow throughout the world shall all return to a single place.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Indeed. Any Mondstadter who leaves their windows open, inviting the company of the wind, shall be guided towards eventual reunion. Let the wind lead, according to his blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Seamus Pegg
dialogues.text: Now, if I may be so bold... Would you hear my confession, Deacon Dahlia?
